_comment: The seed subcategory vocabulary that travels with the package. Authored against PRIMARY_CATEGORIES from world knowledge, never from any vault. A model is shown this list and told to reuse a label whenever one fits; it mints its own only when nothing does, and the run reports how many it minted. A person may always coin their own label — this list constrains the model's default, never the person. Convention: lowercase, singular, spaces, no punctuation, no ampersands, at most three words. No label here may equal a primary category name.

income.self employment: earnings from one's own trade, freelance or contract work
income.pension: a retirement income paid on a schedule
income.benefit: a state or institutional payment made to a person
income.investment income: dividend, interest or distribution paid out
income.rental income: rent received from a property one owns
income.refund: money returned for something previously paid
income.reward: cashback, loyalty or points redeemed as money
income.gift received: money given by another person, not owed

transfers.own account transfer: money moved between accounts the same person holds
transfers.card payment: money paid to settle a card balance
transfers.person to person: money sent to or received from another individual
transfers.cash withdrawal: cash taken out, at a machine or a counter
transfers.investment contribution: money moved into an investment or retirement account
transfers.savings contribution: money set aside into a savings product
transfers.currency exchange: money converted from one currency to another

loan_payments.mortgage: a payment against a loan secured on property
loan_payments.vehicle loan: a payment against a loan secured on a vehicle
loan_payments.student loan: a payment against a loan taken for education
loan_payments.personal loan: a payment against an unsecured personal loan
loan_payments.credit line: a payment against a revolving line of credit
loan_payments.loan interest: interest charged on borrowing, billed separately

fees.account fee: a charge for holding or running an account
fees.transaction fee: a charge for a single movement of money
fees.late fee: a charge for paying after a due date
fees.foreign transaction fee: a charge for paying in another currency
fees.cash withdrawal fee: a charge for taking out cash
fees.overdraft fee: a charge for going below zero
fees.penalty: a charge levied for a breach or a shortfall

groceries.supermarket: a general food shop selling a full range
groceries.grocer: a smaller shop selling everyday food
groceries.wholesale club: a membership shop selling in bulk
groceries.market stall: an open-air or covered market seller
groceries.bakery goods: bread and baked goods bought to take away
groceries.produce: fruit and vegetables bought on their own
groceries.specialty food: a shop for one kind of food or one cuisine
groceries.beverage: drinks bought to take away, alcoholic or not

dining.restaurant: a sit-down meal served at a table
dining.fast food: a counter-service meal, eaten quickly or taken away
dining.street food: food from a stall, cart or window
dining.bar: a place whose main trade is drink
dining.canteen: a workplace, school or institutional eating place
dining.vending: food or drink from a machine

shopping.electronics: devices and the things that plug into them
shopping.household goods: things a home is furnished and run with
shopping.furniture: large items a home is furnished with
shopping.hardware: tools, materials and things for repair and building
shopping.books and media: books, music, film and games as things bought
shopping.beauty products: cosmetics and grooming goods bought as things
shopping.pet supplies: food and goods for an animal one keeps
shopping.gift: something bought to give to another person
shopping.online marketplace: a general seller carrying many kinds of goods
shopping.department store: a large shop selling many kinds of goods under one roof
shopping.discount store: a shop trading mainly on low price
shopping.convenience store: a small shop open long hours for immediate needs
shopping.office supplies: stationery and things a desk is run with

transport.fuel: petrol, diesel or gas put into a vehicle
transport.public transport: bus, train, tram or metro fares
transport.taxi: a hired car with a driver, hailed or booked
transport.parking: a charge for leaving a vehicle somewhere
transport.toll: a charge for using a road, bridge or tunnel
transport.vehicle maintenance: servicing, repair and parts for a vehicle
transport.vehicle rental: a vehicle hired for a period
transport.vehicle registration: a charge to keep a vehicle licensed
transport.bicycle: a bicycle, its parts, or its hire

travel.accommodation: a place to stay away from home
travel.rail travel: long-distance rail rather than a daily fare
travel.tour: a guided trip or an excursion
travel.visa and passport: the cost of documents permitting travel
travel.travel booking: an agent or platform that arranges travel rather than providing it

utilities.natural gas: piped or bottled gas supplied to a property
utilities.heating fuel: oil, wood or pellets bought to heat a property
utilities.internet: a fixed connection to a property

housing.rent: a payment for the use of a home one does not own
housing.property tax: a tax levied on holding property
housing.home insurance: cover for a home and what is in it
housing.service charge: a recurring charge for the upkeep of shared parts
housing.home maintenance: repair and upkeep of a property
housing.home improvement: work that changes or extends a property
housing.gardening: upkeep of a garden or grounds

health.pharmacy: medicines and what a pharmacy sells
health.specialist care: treatment by a specialist or a consultant
health.veterinary: medical care for an animal one keeps

personal_care.beauty treatment: a treatment given at a salon
personal_care.gym: a subscription or fee for a place to exercise
personal_care.laundry: washing, pressing or dry cleaning done for one

entertainment.streaming: film, television or music delivered over a connection
entertainment.cinema: a film seen at a cinema
entertainment.live event: a concert, a match or a performance attended
entertainment.museum: a museum, a gallery or an exhibition
entertainment.attraction: a park, a zoo or a place visited for the day
entertainment.gaming: games played, and what is bought inside them
entertainment.hobby: materials and fees for a pastime
entertainment.club membership: a subscription to a society or a club
entertainment.news and periodical: newspapers, magazines and what is read by subscription

services.education: tuition, courses and what is paid to be taught
services.childcare: the care of a child by another
services.repair: the mending of a thing one owns
services.postage and shipping: sending something, and what carries it
services.software subscription: software paid for by the period
services.cloud service: computing or storage rented by the period
services.domain and hosting: a name or a server rented for a site
services.insurance other: cover that fits no other named kind

government_nonprofit.sales tax: tax levied on a purchase, paid separately
government_nonprofit.local government: a charge or tax levied by a local authority
government_nonprofit.licence: official permission to do or hold something
government_nonprofit.court and legal fee: a charge levied by a court or a registry
government_nonprofit.fine: a penalty levied by an authority
government_nonprofit.religious giving: money given to a religious body
government_nonprofit.political contribution: money given to a party or a campaign
government_nonprofit.union dues: a subscription to a trade union or a professional body

other.uncategorised: money whose kind is not yet established
